title: Compose the J3 restart reconciliation and safe continuation boundary
description:
Objective: compose @moe/runner's committed recovery helpers into a daemon restart boundary that produces J3's four record kinds and a single safe continuation action. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09 from the Foundation canary's block report. This is the LAST unowned M1 exit blocker; J1 is task-671578e5, J4 is task-9011e3b3, and the runner publish it depends on is task-7d0abdcd.

WHAT J3 REQUIRES, design line 1099 - transcribe it rather than trusting this summary: "Kill agent/runner/daemon at declared boundaries. Restart shows adopted, suspect, quarantined, and reconciliation records with truth chips. Healthy continuation is one safe action or an already-approved policy action; it creates a traceable continuation/binding, not edited history."

THE GAP, MEASURED 2026-08-09. The classification logic exists and is complete: @moe/runner's recovery/ subtree provides classifyCrash returning exactly the ADOPTED / ABSENT / SUSPECT / QUARANTINED / RECONCILIATION_COMMAND kinds design 1099 asks for, plus admitSuccessorOverlap, admitResume and advanceRecoveryDrain with their RECOVERY_ERROR_CODES and RECOVERY_LAYERS vocabularies. NOTHING IN THE DAEMON CALLS ANY OF IT. apps/daemon/src/recovery/ contains only doctor-commands.ts, which reports and proposes for an operator; there is no restart path that reads durable records on daemon start and produces the reconciliation record set, and no continuation command.

apps/daemon already declares @moe/runner as a dependency (the approved ownership amendment from task-ba3a45f9 landed), so NO package.json or lockfile change is needed here.

Deliverable: (1) a restart reconciliation service that, given the durable record set, classifies every in-flight attempt through @moe/runner's classifyCrash and persists the resulting adopted / suspect / quarantined / reconciliation records durably, each carrying its truth classification; and (2) a continuation command that is ONE safe action, admitted through admitResume, which APPENDS a traceable continuation binding and never edits prior history.

THE TWO PROPERTIES THAT DEFINE THIS TASK, both from design 1099's second half. Continuation is ONE action - not a sequence a caller must orchestrate, since a partially-orchestrated continuation after a crash is exactly the state J3 exists to prevent. And it creates a BINDING, NOT EDITED HISTORY - the pre-crash records must remain readable and byte-identical after continuation, with the continuation recorded as a successor. A continuation that rewrites the interrupted attempt in place fails J3 even if every other assertion passes.

NOT in scope: new recovery rules in @moe/runner (its recovery subtree is complete and is consumed, not forked); the killing of processes, which belongs to the E2E canary harness; J1 or J4; doctor-commands.ts behaviour, which already reports and proposes correctly; any HTTP or transport change.

Hard dependencies: task-7d0abdcd (Publish the runner recovery, evidence and Claude observation surfaces on the @moe/runner root). Until it lands, classifyCrash and admitResume are unreachable from outside @moe/runner because its exports map is exclusive - a deep subpath import will not resolve at runtime.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/** (additions only - do not rewrite doctor-commands.ts) and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts (command-kind vocabulary only).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: A restart reconciliation service classifies every in-flight attempt in the durable record set through @moe/runner's classifyCrash and persists the outcome, producing records for all four kinds design 1099 names — adopted, suspect, quarantined and reconciliation — each carrying its truth classification. The outcome-kind set is asserted by set equality against @moe/runner's exported RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS, and the seeded case count is asserted non-zero so a sweep that classifies nothing cannot pass.

Nothing silently resumes: every in-flight attempt lands in exactly one classified record, and there is no code path that returns an attempt to running without a classified record and an explicit continuation. Assert the total classification, including that an attempt whose state cannot be established becomes SUSPECT rather than adopted.

Continuation is ONE safe action: a single command admitted through @moe/runner's admitResume moves a reconciled attempt forward, and a resume attempted across an unproven safe boundary refuses with the runner's own RECOVERY_ERROR_CODES value and the refusing layer, committing NOTHING — proven by reading the store back, not by the returned value.

Continuation creates a BINDING, NOT EDITED HISTORY: after a continuation, the pre-crash records remain retrievable and BYTE-IDENTICAL, with the continuation recorded as a traceable successor. Assert by capturing the prior record's bytes before continuation and comparing after — asserting only that a new record appeared would pass against an in-place rewrite, which is the defect this DoD exists to catch.

Restart reconciliation is idempotent: running it twice over the same durable state produces the same records and leaves exactly one row per attempt, asserted by reading row counts back rather than by the second run not throwing.

Every refusal surfaces @moe/runner's own recovery reason code and layer rather than a locally invented one, so which layer refused survives the composition — asserted by feeding a case the runner's helpers reject and pinning that exact code.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, and only owned paths are staged and committed by explicit pathspec.
taskRails: Compose, never decide. Every recovery rule lives in @moe/runner's recovery subtree already. A daemon module that re-implements crash classification or safe-boundary admission creates a second source of truth that will drift from the one the supervisor hardening gate drilled; if a rule seems missing, report_blocked rather than writing it here.

Import @moe/runner from its package ROOT specifier only — never a deep subpath. Its exports map is exclusive and deep imports do not resolve at runtime; that wall is precisely why task-7d0abdcd exists and is this task's hard dependency.

History is append-only. Continuation appends a successor binding and never rewrites, deletes or reclassifies the interrupted attempt. Prove prior records are still byte-identical afterwards, not merely that a new record was created.

Nothing silently resumes. There must be no path from crashed to running that skips a classified record and an explicit continuation — the absence of such a path is the point of J3, so assert it rather than assuming it.
Uncertainty stays SUSPECT. An attempt whose state cannot be established is never optimistically adopted; unverifiable evidence must not gain authority.
Assert the reason code AND the refusing layer, and prove non-mutation by reading the store back — a handler that mutates then refuses passes a return-value-only assertion.
Do not rewrite doctor-commands.ts. It already reports and proposes correctly for an operator; this task adds the restart and continuation path beside it.

Any new module needs its sibling .js bridge in the same commit — apps/daemon is bridged and covered by the repo-wide runtime-loadability gate. Keep each production source under 250 lines, split before 400, and commit by explicit pathspec only; sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/ and http/ in the same tree.

DESIGN LINE 1099 TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM: "J3 - crash recovery. Kill agent/runner/daemon at declared boundaries. Restart shows adopted, suspect, quarantined, and reconciliation records with truth chips. Healthy continuation is one safe action or an already-approved policy action; it creates a traceable continuation/binding, not edited history."
Two halves: (1) restart produces the four record kinds with truth chips; (2) continuation is ONE safe action creating a traceable binding, NOT edited history.

VOCABULARIES READ FROM packages/runner/src/recovery/recovery-contract.ts:
- RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS = ADOPTED, ABSENT, SUSPECT, QUARANTINED, RECONCILIATION_COMMAND. FIVE, not four. Design 1099 names four (adopted/suspect/quarantined/reconciliation); the runner adds ABSENT. I will assert set equality against the EXPORTED list, per DoD 1, and note the design-vs-vocabulary difference rather than silently reconciling it — ABSENT is a classification, not a resume, so it does not weaken "nothing silently resumes". Confirmed there is NO RESUMED arm, which is what makes that property checkable.
- RECOVERY_LAYERS = SAFE_BOUNDARY | CLASSIFICATION.
- RECOVERY_ERROR_CODES = 9 codes. The contract's own comment records why RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_ACTIVE and RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_RELEASE_UNKNOWN are separate: "we know it has not released" and "we cannot tell whether it released" are different facts, and collapsing them would let an operator read an unverifiable boundary as a verified one. That is exactly DoD 3's three-predecessor-state requirement, so I will pin those two codes distinctly.
- PREDECESSOR_RELEASES = PROVEN_RELEASED | ACTIVE | UNKNOWN.
- admitResume refuses unless predecessorRelease === "PROVEN_RELEASED" AND safeHandoff !== null, with RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN at layer SAFE_BOUNDARY. classifyCrash refuses a stale observation with RECOVERY_STALE_OBSERVATION_REFUSED and takes an exact-keyed {records, observation, authority} record.
- The contract also documents UNESTABLISHED as first-class and never collapsing into PROVEN_ABSENT, which is task rail 5's "uncertainty stays SUSPECT" already enforced upstream.

implementationPlan.description: Prove restart reconciliation is idempotent — DoD 5, which is not optional because this path runs on EVERY daemon start. Run reconciliation twice over the same durable state and assert the produced records are identical and that exactly ONE row exists per attempt, reading the row counts back from the store rather than trusting that the second run did not throw — 'it did not throw' is precisely what a duplicate-write also looks like. Then the harder case: run reconciliation, apply a legitimate change, and run it again, asserting it converges on the new correct classification rather than either duplicating records or refusing to update. A reconciliation that is idempotent only over unchanged state is not idempotent in the way a restart path needs.
implementationPlan.note:
Idempotence proven by reading durable rows back, not by "the second run did not throw".

restart-reconciliation-idempotence.test.ts, 2 cases:
1. UNCHANGED STATE. Two attempts (ADOPTED seed + SUSPECT seed via lockState UNKNOWN), reconcileOnRestart run twice over the same durable store. Asserts first toEqual second, AND reads the raw decision log back through readCommandDecisionsAfter filtered to commandKind reconciliation.decide, asserting exactly attempts.length rows — one row per attempt, not "no throw". This assertion is load-bearing: without commitRecord's byte-equality short circuit the second run would re-attempt expectedVersion=0 against an aggregate already at v1, the store would refuse, and reconcileOnRestart would return ok:false — reddening the toEqual as well as the count.
2. CONVERGENCE AFTER A LEGITIMATE CHANGE — the harder arm the step demanded. Same attemptRef reconciled first as ADOPTED, then with lockState UNKNOWN so the runner reclassifies it SUSPECT, then replayed. Asserts the classification actually moved ADOPTED -> SUSPECT (converges rather than refusing to update), that the third run equals the second (idempotent at the NEW state, not only at the original one), that the read-back map holds SUSPECT, and that the decision log holds exactly 2 rows — one per real version, so convergence did not duplicate.

Note on row counting: readReconciliationRecords returns a Map keyed by attemptRef and would collapse duplicates, so both cases assert against the raw decision rows instead. Counting the map alone would have been the vacuous version of this test.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test: 23 files / 464 tests passed.

continuation-service.test.ts pins DoD 3 plus the ONE-action property:

ONE ACTION, counted rather than implied. A single evaluateContinuationCommandBytes call moves a reconciled attempt forward; the test asserts CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KINDS has length 1 (the surface offers exactly one continuation action, so there is no second command a caller could be left owing) AND that the durable decision-row count rose by exactly 1 across that one call. Every refusal asserts the runner's own code AND layer "SAFE_BOUNDARY", and the codes are also asserted to be members of the runner's exported RECOVERY_ERROR_CODES rather than string literals the daemon invented.

admitResume IS LOAD-BEARING: a fourth case sends PROVEN_RELEASED with safeHandoff null. admitSuccessorOverlap ADMITS that request; only admitResume refuses it (RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN). A composition that called the overlap helper and skipped the resume helper is red here and green everywhere else.

COMMITS NOTHING, proven by reading the store back. Every refusal case snapshots all durable rows (commandId, kind, target aggregate, version, disposition, resultBytes) before the call and asserts the snapshot is byte-identical after. A handler that wrote first and refused second passes a return-value-only assertion; it cannot pass this one.

NOTHING RESUMES WITHOUT A CLASSIFIED RECORD: two daemon-layer gates, each with its own code and both asserted to have refused at layer "CONTINUATION" rather than "SAFE_BOUNDARY" — an attempt restart reconciliation never saw (CONTINUATION_ATTEMPT_UNRECONCILED) and an attempt whose classification the runner itself REFUSED (CONTINUATION_ATTEMPT_UNCLASSIFIED). The second closes the hole where a record exists but carries no classification.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/recovery/continuation-service.ts to green, APPEND-ONLY — DoD 4, and the property the obvious implementation breaks. 'Continue the interrupted attempt' reads naturally as updating that attempt's row; design 1099 requires a traceable continuation BINDING and says explicitly 'not edited history'. So the continuation APPENDS a successor binding that references the interrupted attempt, and the interrupted attempt's record is never rewritten, deleted or reclassified. Assert it the strong way: capture the prior record's stored bytes before continuation, then after, and assert byte-identical — asserting only that a new record appeared would pass against an in-place rewrite, which is the exact defect this DoD exists to catch. Follow the house handler shape (bounded decode, exact-shape gate with pinned schemaVersion, call admitResume, commit only on acceptance, frozen discriminated result), append the new command kind to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS rather than reordering it, and add the module's .js bridge in the same commit.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test -> 26 files / 480 tests passed. Both new modules have their sibling .js bridges (`export * from "./<name>.ts";`, matching restart-reconciliation.js).

SHAPE. Split at write time because one module came to 352 lines, over the 250 target: continuation-contracts.ts (232) holds the vocabulary, the result union and the byte ingress; continuation-service.ts (169) holds the flow. Every production file in recovery/ is now under 250: contracts 232, service 169, restart-reconciliation 210, doctor-commands 229 (untouched).

APPEND-ONLY, and the one seam that decides it. `bindingTarget(binding)` returns BOTH the aggregate id and the expected version from one place — a fresh aggregate named for the SUCCESSOR, always at version 0. Splitting those across two call-site arguments is what would let them drift; keeping them together makes "where may a continuation write" a single line to read and a single line to drill in step 7. The interrupted attempt's reconciliation aggregate is never a target, never re-committed, never reclassified.

DoD 4 asserted the strong way, in continuation-binding.test.ts, TWO ways it could be broken: the record as read back through readReconciliationRecords is byte-identical across the continuation, AND the raw durable rows written under RESTART_RECONCILIATION_COMMAND_KIND are identical in target, version and bytes. The second is the one that catches a rewrite that happens to be undecodable as a reconciliation record — the map-level assertion alone would silently pass that. The command kind is now exported from restart-reconciliation.ts rather than restated in the test, so the filter cannot drift from what production writes.

ONE REAL BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT. The first implementation checked only `response.decision.effectDisposition`. That field is "EFFECTS_COMMITTED" on a REPLAYED commit too, because the store returns the HISTORICAL decision — so a second continuation naming the same successor with a different handoff returned ok:true describing a binding that was never written. Fixed by comparing the returned resultBytes against the proposed bytes: identical bytes mean the one action was retried verbatim and stays BOUND (a crash between issuing and observing must not become an error), different bytes mean a different continuation is claiming that successor and it refuses CONTINUATION_BINDING_CONFLICT. Both arms are now pinned by test, and both assert the durable snapshot is unchanged.

COMPOSED, NOT RESTATED. classifyCrash, admitSuccessorOverlap, admitResume, RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS and PREDECESSOR_RELEASES all come from the @moe/runner ROOT specifier. The release lattice is validated against the runner's exported PREDECESSOR_RELEASES rather than a local copy, so a member added there cannot be silently accepted or dropped here. Boundary refusals carry the runner's code, layer and message out verbatim via boundaryRefusal; the daemon's own four codes are all raised at layer "CONTINUATION" so a reader can tell the two apart.

TEST SPLIT. The suite reached 335 lines, over the role's 300 cap, so it is now continuation-service.test.ts (191: one-action, the three predecessor states, the two daemon gates, ingress) plus continuation-binding.test.ts (93: append-only) over a shared continuation-test-harness.ts (103). The harness DRIVES the production surface and restates nothing — seed calls the real reconcileOnRestart, run calls the real command entry point, and no classification, admission or refusal code is re-derived there.

DEVIATION AS FLAGGED IN STEP 5: CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KINDS lives in the owned recovery module with `satisfies readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]` instead of being appended to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, which would have forced edits in five files owned by sibling tasks (bootstrap-sequence.ts, bootstrap-services.test.ts, bootstrap-durability.test.ts, goals/j1-command-path.test.ts, bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts). bootstrap-contracts.ts is therefore UNMODIFIED by this task.

implementationPlan.description: Prove the guards are load-bearing, then run the gates. MUTATION DRILL at each mechanism's single source: the append-only guard in continuation, the admitResume pass-through, the SUSPECT-never-adopted branch, the totality of classification, and the expected-version check. Neutralise each operand with a constant — NEVER delete a line, since a deleted line from a multi-line condition is a syntax error that reddens the suite for the wrong reason and proves nothing. Count failed SUITES as well as failed tests and confirm the red test is the one naming that guard's code. TWO MUTATIONS DECIDE THIS TASK: removing the append-only guard must redden the byte-identity assertion, and replacing the classification totality with a partial mapping must redden the outcome-set equality — if either survives, that DoD is untested however green the suite looks. This worktree is shared and another agent's completion hook can commit your mutation, so capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` before each drill and verify the restore against that sha rather than `git status`. Then run fresh: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck, all exiting 0, and confirm both new modules have their .js bridges.
implementationPlan.note:
FIVE DRILLS RUN. Files are UNTRACKED in this shared tree, so `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` has nothing to compare against; restores were verified against sha256 of a pre-drill copy held outside the repo (`sha256sum -c`, OK on every restore). No mutation deleted a line — each replaced one operand with a constant.

DRILL 1, APPEND-ONLY — SURVIVED FIRST, AND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN TEST. `bindingTarget` returned the attempt's reconciliation aggregate at version 1 instead of a fresh successor aggregate at 0, i.e. the continuation wrote straight into the interrupted attempt's history. Suite stayed 26/26 GREEN. Cause: my byte-identity helper filtered durable rows by COMMAND KIND, and the injected write carried the continuation's own kind ("work.resume"), so the very row that edited history was excluded from the comparison — the assertion had quietly detached from the thing it was written to catch. Fixed by keying the comparison on TARGET AGGREGATE instead, with the aggregate id now exported from production as `reconciliationAggregateId(attemptRef)` rather than restated as a literal in the test. Re-ran the identical mutation: `Test Files 1 failed | 25 passed`, `Tests 1 failed`, and the one red test is "leaves the pre-crash record byte-identical and records the continuation as a successor". This is the mutation the plan said decides the task.

DRILL 2, admitResume pass-through. `if (resume.kind === "REFUSED")` -> `if (false)`. 1 suite / 1 test red: "refuses a proven release carrying no safe handoff, so admitResume is load-bearing". Confirms the second runner admission is genuinely reached — the overlap helper ADMITS that case, so only admitResume can refuse it.

DRILL 3, SUSPECT-never-adopted AND classification totality. `recordBase(result.kind, attemptRef)` -> `recordBase("ADOPTED", attemptRef)`. 4 suites / 10 tests red, including the outcome-set equality test ("produces exactly the runner's outcome kinds over a non-empty seeded sweep"), BOTH "uncertainty stays suspect" tests, all three refusal-code tests, and the continuation gate that refuses an unclassified attempt. This is the second mutation the plan said decides the task: a partial mapping cannot survive.

DRILL 4, classification vocabulary. `...RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS` -> `...RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS.slice(0, 4)`. 1 suite / 2 tests red: the vocabulary derivation test and the durable truth-chip test — dropping a kind from the accepted set makes RECONCILIATION_COMMAND records undecodable on read-back, and both assertions catch it.

DRILL 5, expected-version check. `const expectedVersion = current?.version ?? 0;` -> `= 0`. 1 suite / 1 test red: "converges after a legitimate state change and does not duplicate the converged row" — exactly the idempotence arm that only a changed-state replay can reach.

- pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck -> exit 0

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, each question answered against the code rather than the intent:

- Path from crashed to running that skips a classified record? None. The only writer of a continuation binding is evaluateContinuationCommandBytes, and it refuses before any commit unless readReconciliationRecords returns a record for that attempt whose classification is a member of the runner's RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS. Reconciliation itself cannot resume anything: the vocabulary it can produce has no RESUMED arm, so a silent resume is unexpressible rather than merely unchecked.
- Can an unestablished attempt be adopted through any route, including a default branch? No. recordOf forwards classifyCrash's own kind; there is no default arm and no local re-derivation. Drill 3 confirms — substituting the constant "ADOPTED" reddens 4 suites / 10 tests including both "uncertainty stays suspect" cases.
- Can a continuation rewrite, delete or reclassify the interrupted attempt's record? No, and this is now proven rather than asserted: bindingTarget is the only place a write target is chosen, and the drill that pointed it at the attempt's aggregate reddens the byte-identity test by name.
- Does continuation take ONE command? Yes — one kind in the vocabulary, one entry point, one durable row per call, and the test counts all three rather than checking the end state is reachable.
- Any recovery rule restated in the daemon? No. classifyCrash, admitSuccessorOverlap, admitResume, RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS and PREDECESSOR_RELEASES are all consumed; the request parser validates the release lattice against the runner's exported list, not a local copy.
- Deep subpath import of @moe/runner? None: `grep -rn "@moe/runner/" apps/daemon/src/` returns nothing. Additionally the three bridged modules were LOADED in a plain Node process (node --experimental-strip-types, run from apps/daemon) and resolved their @moe/runner root imports at runtime, so the wall vitest would have hidden is checked directly.
- Locally invented code where the runner's should have survived? No. boundaryRefusal carries the runner's code, layer and message verbatim; the four daemon codes cover ingress and the daemon's own gates, which have no runner equivalent, and all four are raised at layer "CONTINUATION" so the two layers stay distinguishable.
- Duplicate rows on a second reconciliation? No — proven by reading row counts back, on unchanged state AND after a legitimate reclassification.
- doctor-commands.ts modified? No. It is absent from the change set; it still reports and proposes for an operator, and continuation now APPLIES the same "work.resume" operation it proposes.

COMMIT — READ THIS, IT IS NOT THE NORMAL SHAPE. There is no commit of this task's own. Between the gate run and the staging step, a sibling task's completion hook (task-9011e3b3, J4) swept the whole working tree and committed all twelve of these files inside `5ef4bcc feat(task-9011e3b32c414e9ca0d49f49fdfaaf08): Persist the review flow...`. By the time `git add -- <twelve explicit paths>` ran there was nothing left to stage, and `git diff --cached --name-only` was empty. I did not amend the foreign commit, did not create an empty commit, and did not stage anything foreign — the staged index was verified empty before and after.

QA should review by `git diff 7afa17d..HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/recovery/`, which lists exactly the twelve owned files and nothing else.

EIGHT PITFALLS, all measured on disk today:
1. RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS HAS FIVE ARMS, NOT FOUR — [ADOPTED, ABSENT, SUSPECT, QUARANTINED, RECONCILIATION_COMMAND]. Design 1099 names four; the runner adds ABSENT. DoD 1 says assert set equality against the EXPORTED list, so assert five and record the difference rather than narrowing to four. The list has NO RESUMED arm, which is exactly what makes "nothing silently resumes" checkable.
2. classifyCrash takes an EXACT-KEYED record {records, observation, claimedAuthority}. The third key is claimedAuthority, NOT "authority" as the task description says — the exactRecord gate turns a wrong key into RECOVERY_BOUNDARY_MALFORMED rather than a useful error.
3. CrashClassification is a SIX-arm union: ADOPTED{effectRef,postState}, ABSENT{effectRef}, SUSPECT{effectRef,postState}, QUARANTINED{effectRef,held[]}, RECONCILIATION_COMMAND{effectRef,command,detail}, REFUSED{failure}. REFUSED is NOT an outcome kind — do not count it as a classification.
4. admitResume refuses unless predecessorRelease === "PROVEN_RELEASED" AND safeHandoff !== null, with RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN at layer SAFE_BOUNDARY. PREDECESSOR_RELEASES = [PROVEN_RELEASED, ACTIVE, UNKNOWN]; the contract's own comment says RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_ACTIVE and RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_RELEASE_UNKNOWN are deliberately distinct because "we know it has not released" and "we cannot tell" are different facts. That IS DoD 3's three-state requirement — pin both codes distinctly.
5. classifyCrash refuses a stale observation (observedEpoch < records.intent.leaseBinding.epoch) with RECOVERY_STALE_OBSERVATION_REFUSED. Easy to trip by accident when hand-building fixtures.
6. FIXTURES: packages/runner/src/recovery/recovery-test-fixtures.ts has situation()/observation()/records() plus a SETTLED terminal override showing a valid shape. It is TEST-TIER — no .js bridge, not on the runner root — so you cannot import it from the daemon. Read it and hand-build the equivalent.

Coordination posted in #general msg-a96a486cdd864c75a3d477164894f2f2: APPEND to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, never reorder, one line each, explicit per-file pathspec. NEVER a directory pathspec under apps/daemon/src/ — bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/ and recovery/ have different owners right now.

Foreign completion hooks committed my owned files mid-task on all three of my previous tasks, and repo-wide gate legs are intermittently red on other agents' in-flight files. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) THE TWO HALVES SHARE A TASK because they share the same durable record set and the same store transaction discipline, and because splitting them would let restart reconciliation land without any way to act on its output — a board full of SUSPECT records and no continuation command is worse than neither. They are also both small: this is composition over @moe/runner's finished recovery subtree.
(2) THE HARD DEPENDENCY IS REAL AND MUST BE CHECKED AT STEP 1, not assumed. task-7d0abdcd publishes classifyCrash / admitResume / advanceRecoveryDrain on the @moe/runner root. Until it lands they are unreachable: the exports map is exclusive and a deep subpath does not resolve at runtime. If a worker reaches for a deep import to get moving, this task ships a runtime failure that vitest will hide — the exact wall that has cost this board several task-days.
(3) APPEND-ONLY IS THE PROPERTY MOST LIKELY TO BE IMPLEMENTED WRONG, because the natural way to 'continue an interrupted attempt' is to update that attempt's row. Design 1099 requires a traceable continuation BINDING and explicitly says 'not edited history'. I gave it its own step and a byte-comparison assertion, because a test that only checks 'a new record exists' passes against an in-place rewrite.
(4) NOTHING SILENTLY RESUMES IS ASSERTED AS AN ABSENCE, which is hard to test well. The plan does it two ways: totality (every in-flight attempt lands in exactly one classified record) and a vocabulary check (the outcome kinds equal @moe/runner's exported RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS, which deliberately contains no RESUMED arm). Together those make a silent resume unexpressible rather than merely untested.

**Dependency edge is already in place**: apps/daemon/package.json declares @moe/contracts, @moe/core, @moe/runner, @moe/scheduler, @moe/store. The @moe/runner edge landed with task-ba3a45f9's approved amendment, so NO package.json or lockfile change is needed here — do not add one.
**What the daemon already has, and must not be rewritten**: `apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-commands.ts` — DOCTOR_RECOVERY_SCHEMA_VERSION, DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS, DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES, evaluateDoctorCommandBytes (:215), and the result union DoctorInputRejected | DoctorRequestInvalid | DoctorAuthorityStale | DoctorReported | DoctorProposed. It REPORTS and PROPOSES for an operator and deliberately does not repair; this task adds the restart and continuation path BESIDE it and reuses its refusal shape where sensible.
**House handler shape**, stated at `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:48`: 'One shape for every project command: reduce, then commit only on acceptance.' Concretely: bounded decode, exact-shape gate against a frozen key list with a pinned schemaVersion, call the pure layer, commit through the store, return a frozen discriminated union.
**Durability seam**: @moe/store's `commitExpectedVersionDecision` gives one durable terminal decision with disposition REPLAYED on replay — that is what the idempotence DoD rides on; `readCommandDecisionsAfter` is the read-back path for proving non-mutation.
**Design authority**: line 1099. Read it directly (read-only — epic rail 1).
planningNotes.risks:
1. **If task-7d0abdcd has not landed, the runner recovery symbols are unreachable and the honest response is to block, not to deep-import.** A deep subpath typechecks and passes vitest while failing at runtime under Node — this repo has lost several task-days to exactly that, and it would be invisible to this task's own gate.
2. **Append-only will be broken by the obvious implementation.** 'Continue the interrupted attempt' naturally reads as updating that attempt's row. Capture the prior record's bytes before continuation and compare after; 'a new record appeared' passes against an in-place rewrite.
3. **A silent resume is an absence, and absences are easy to test badly.** Rely on totality plus the vocabulary: RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS has no RESUMED arm, so assert the daemon's produced kinds equal that exported list rather than a local copy, and assert every in-flight attempt lands in exactly one record.
4. **Do not optimistically adopt.** An attempt whose state cannot be established is SUSPECT. The tempting bug is treating 'the process looks alive' or 'no error was recorded' as adoption — both are quiescence, not proof.
5. **Restart reconciliation runs on every daemon start, so idempotence is not optional**: two runs over the same durable state must produce identical records and exactly one row per attempt, asserted by reading counts back.
6. **Surface the runner's own codes and layers**, never local ones — RECOVERY_LAYERS distinguishes SAFE_BOUNDARY from CLASSIFICATION, and collapsing that loses which layer refused.
7. **Do not rewrite doctor-commands.ts**; it is a sibling concern that already works, and its owner may still be active.
8. Commit hazard: sibling tasks own bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/ and http/ in the same tree — never a directory pathspec under apps/daemon/src/.
